title: IP Addresses and DNS
text: An IP (Internet Protocol) address is a unique numerical identifier assigned to each device on a network, enabling it to send and receive data. IPv4 addresses (e.g., 192.168.1.1) use a 32-bit format with about 4.3 billion possible addresses, while the newer IPv6 offers a vastly larger address space. The Domain Name System (DNS) acts like a phonebook, translating memorable domain names into IP addresses.
